cases.reason: Strongest reading tried: 2023 SR15 carries a second sentence (at least one body group) that 1985 might not require, and the census case shows no rule that depends on the body-group class. Neither holds: 1985 TYPE SR7 states the same requirement, so the pointer's whole verdict is true of the 1985 scope; the census case runs at 85 accepted with DE, CH and CF groups. The classification itself is also correct at 85: probe bodynp.cob (LINE ... ON NEXT PAGE in CH, DE and CF, allowed only in body groups by 1985 LINE SR7) is accepted and runs (BODYNP OK); phnp.cob, the same with a PAGE HEADING using NEXT PAGE, is refused COBOL2199 citing XIII.3.15.3 SR7. That pair is a stronger own witness than the census case, if one is wanted.

cases.attempt: A program whose result depends on what 'access mode' means, apart from what the ACCESS MODE clause and the I-O statement rules say for each mode.
cases.reason: None found. The row names the concept and its subject is a file of the user's program. Every observable behaviour (which statements are allowed, sequential or random retrieval) is stated by the ACCESS MODE clause and statement rows.

cases.attempt: A program declaring ALTERNATE RECORD KEY on the prime key's item, to show 'other than the prime record key'.
cases.reason: That program is refused under §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR4 (cite_check OK: 'must not reference an item whose leftmost character position corresponds'), its own row. The definition itself requires nothing further.

cases.attempt: probes\g-01-refute\blkfile.cob: write 3 records to a file with BLOCK CONTAINS 5 RECORDS, read it back and count them. A compiler that let block size shape file size (padding to a whole block, so extra records come back) would break the row's third sentence, 'The size of a block has no direct relationship to the size of the file' (cite_check OK §1985:III.2 p17).
cases.reason: The row has more than a definition: sentences 2-3 state properties of the medium (a block may hold part of a logical record; block size is unrelated to file and record size), and a program can see a violation. Its subject is also the implementation's physical medium, not the user's program, which the definitional arm excludes. At 85 the compiler is correct: BLKFILE OK 3 (run E:\COBOL-coord\scratch\w20262131o\runs\blkfile-001). The row needs an own witness, not a derivation.

cases.attempt: A program whose outcome depends on 'combined at object time', such as a CALL that must resolve at run time.
cases.reason: The run-time resolution and the effects of CALL are the CALL statement's GRs, in their own rows. This row names a role in the user's run unit and adds nothing a program could see.
It names a role in the user's run unit, and no outcome depends on it.

cases.attempt: A program using a cd-name in a way that tests the definition.
cases.reason: The form and use of a cd-name are stated by the CD entry rows. This row defines the class of user-defined word, a property of the user's program.

cases.attempt: A program that depends on what counts as a clause.
cases.reason: Each clause's format and rules are separate rows. This row defines a unit of the user's source and requires nothing.

cases.attempt: Read 'complete' as closing the set: a program at 85 that uses a character outside the set outside literals and comments must be refused.
cases.reason: That closure is stated as its own requirement in §1985:IV.4.1 p1 (cite_check OK: 'The character set consists of the characters as defined under COBOL Character Set'), together with the literal and comment expansion. The members are the T7 rows. The lead requires nothing beyond those rows.

cases.attempt: A program whose comparisons, SORT/MERGE or sequential indexed retrieval depend on the definition.
cases.reason: Each of the four uses is a separate rule (the comparison rules, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SORT/MERGE, READ NEXT ordering). The row only names the ordering they apply.

cases.attempt: No program witness written. The attack is on the arm's precondition.
cases.reason: The subject of the row is not the user's program. It is an external mechanism: 'A mechanism (hardware or hardware/software)... This mechanism may be a computer or a peripheral device' (cite_check OK §1985:III.2 p38 on 'This mechanism may be a computer or a peripheral device'). The definitional arm requires a property OF THE USER'S PROGRAM and never one of the implementation or environment. The names given recast the subject as the device. Only the third sentence touches programs with CD entries. The arm does not fit, so the row needs another arm (informative about the environment, if every sentence qualifies) or a Communication-module witness of the third sentence.

cases.attempt: Read the subject as the implementation's translation phase, not the user's program, and look for a program whose result depends on the term.
cases.reason: Rules that act 'at compile time' are their own rows. The term qualifies when the user's source program is translated. No program outcome depends on this row alone.

cases.attempt: A program whose result depends on 'contiguous items' apart from the rules that use the term.
cases.reason: The rules that use the term state the behaviour. This row defines a relationship among items of the user's program.

cases.attempt: A program depending on what a control data-name is.
cases.reason: The CONTROL clause rows state the form and the control-break behaviour. This row names a role in the user's report.

cases.attempt: A program whose result depends on a data item being a 'counter'.
cases.reason: The arithmetic, SUM and SET rows state the behaviour. This row names a use of a data item of the user's program.

cases.attempt: A program showing that the record area holds the record after a READ.
cases.reason: That is a READ general rule, in its own row. This row names the record available in the record area of a user's file.

cases.attempt: A program depending on what counts as a data clause.
cases.reason: Each data clause is a separate set of rows. This row names a category of clause in the user's program.

cases.attempt: A program depending on 'excluding literals' or on function values being data items.
cases.reason: The rows that use the term state the behaviour for literals and for functions. This row defines a category in the user's program.
